title: I made a little AI trading coach, curious what you think
author: TradeCoach_

comments.author: Interesting_Gold_792
comments.body:
Interesting idea. How are you separating a bad trade from a good trade that simply had a losing outcome?

I’m working on an automated system, and that distinction has become pretty important for me. A loss doesn’t necessarily mean the decision was wrong if the setup, risk and execution were all valid.

replies.author: TradeCoach_
replies.body:
Good question

TradeCoach doesn't grade whether you made money. It grades the decision making that was visible before the outcome happened. The four things it scores every trade on are:

\- Risk management- was your position size/risk % actually reasonable for the setup  
\- Entry timing — was it a real confirmed signal, or a reactive chase  
\- Exit timing — did you manage the exit well relative to the full move  
\- R:R ratio — was the risk:reward you set up actually favorable

P&L shows up in the app because obviously you want to see it, but it's not one of the four graded categories. It's just used as evidence to explain why something was a good or bad decision (e.g. "you risked 18% of your account on a low-probability setup" — that's a knock on risk management, regardless of whether that trade happened to work out).

So yeah, you can take a well-sized, well-timed trade with a good stop and still lose, and it'll grade out fine (B/A range), because the process was sound and variance just didn't go your way. And you can YOLO into something, get lucky, and still get graded a D because the decision itself was bad even though the outcome was green.
